# Phase directive — «First readings on the standing rig» (Epoch 4's head entry, viola-0.2.0)

1. Scope is the route entry and its SIX carries as they stand at `88e310ba`, nothing wider: R3 (a fired scheduled
   wake's `source` field, «a real wake reads 1», the hook-latency window of v2-19), R4 (the live `viola verify
   --record`, with the record-home rule's live half), the external-imports modal read live, R2's unexplained
   `box-text: holds-text`, and the nextest kill-line carry. Every live reading runs on the COMMITTED rig
   `viola-live-rig` as chunk 2026-11-17-standing-live-rig left it; a reading the rig cannot take as built is named
   with what the rig lacks — the rig is extended only as far as a reading needs.
2. **Which CLI a start runs — measured by the overseer on this host, 2026-11-17:** PATH `claude` is 2.1.326 (mise
   `latest` moved); the live home's stamps hold 2.1.296 · .302 · .312 · .319 · .323 · .325 and NOT .326; the 2.1.325
   install is `~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.325/claude` (no `bin/`). So a start that takes PATH `claude`
   runs a version no stamp covers. At P3 say for each reading which binary it starts and why; a reading on 2.1.326
   and R4's stamping of it are named apart from the readings on 2.1.325, each with its own count.
3. **SIZE FIRST.** At P3's END, before P4, stop with ONE block:
   (a) whether every carried reading plus the nextest step fits one implement window (say your own window at that
   point), and if not, a split named plainly — what stays and what goes to a following entry; the placement is the
   founder's, do not take it;
   (b) the live starts: for each reading the SHAPE first (what makes the screen or the event appear, what closes it,
   who holds the wheel at the key, what the start reads if the thing does not show — R3's wake must FIRE inside the
   start, so say how long the start stands and what bounds it), then the exact count, the keys the rig types into
   its own pty (a key into the external-imports modal is asked, never assumed), and what the chunk loses without
   each;
   (c) R4 by itself: what a live `viola verify --record` starts (how many `claude` starts it is by the product's own
   count), what it writes and where (a record home from a helper, no path component named `home`), and that nothing
   of the live home's stamps moves.
   The cap, the keys and a split's placement are the founder's, per chunk; the overseer brings them to him in one
   dialog. Plan every other step on the fake agent meanwhile.
4. **The builder sets NO scheduled wake or timer of its own — and R3 needs one FIRED.** The wake R3 reads is set
   inside the rig's OWN started session (its `claude`, in its pty), never in this session; say in (b) exactly what
   that session is asked to do and that this session's wake guard is not what refuses or admits it.
5. **The nextest carry's fork, technical, decided here:** `cli` and `harness_tied` join the `ci` 20 s kill line as
   they are; for `harness_lifecycle`, propose at P4 between shortening the readiness deadline that
   `boot_that_never_gets_ready_times_out_and_stops_its_supervisor` waits out (20.644 s measured) and a bound of its
   own for that binary — with the measured wall after the change, and never by adding the binary and letting the
   kill line end that case.
6. The rig's isolation stands as built: a scratch root outside every repository, a private config dir, the
   credentials copy guarded by the token-window read (a start refused under 20 minutes of token left is uncounted —
   stop and say so, no timer) and removed on every exit path; the screen kept LOCALLY, closed words only in a
   record; nothing of his status line or config in a commit. Each start is ledgered with the clock's time before it
   is made.
7. No mutation run. Name each control's `--timeout S` in the plan's prose AND fire it with that flag, on an entry
   filtered to the guard's own cases; a control id stays within 16 characters; «holds» = those cases ran and FAILED
   with no TIMEOUT line. Every acceptance predicate is one that CAN fail — the last chunk's `vfy-tie` control did
   not hold as planned because an untied verify ended by itself inside the bound: for each control say what the
   subject does when the guard is gone, measured or marked unmeasured.
8. A gate entry that names an installed tool's path is checked against the host before the card. A change to the
   fake agent's screens puts `cli_verify` in the gate block. A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint.
9. A fold is decided at the PHASE. If implement meets a red that moves a plan entry it stops and says so BEFORE the
   operator pass.
10. A fork that is the founder's (a boundary widening, a live cap, a typed key, a placement) is asked through the
    overseer, who brings it to him by dialog — he is present, slow to answer; a technical fork is answered by relay
    at once.
11. End every process you start.
12. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the
    union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; rows read whole or by search; whether EVERY cited row is in
    the union or its standing list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` /
    `INDETERMINATE` / `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

     capture line's `ms`; `unmeasured` when either is missing), `screen-ms` (the fired line's `ts` less the wall clock

     stand bound the start reads `wake: unfired`, `capture-source: unread`, `latency-ms: unmeasured`.

body:
# P5 review — «First readings on the standing rig», plan of 2026-11-17T16:13:55Z

The plan stands but for one gap that would spend `R3-326` — the one start with no spare — on a reading it cannot
return. Technical, the overseer's; no founder fork in it. Revise the plan on these three points, then put the card
again.

1. **`R3-326` on a transport-only wrapper — say from the PRODUCT'S CODE what that start can read, and make the arm
   follow it.** The plan's own note says `viola run` on an unstamped CLI is transport-only. The R3 arm finds the
   fired wake by a `prompt-submitted` line with no send in flight, and waits `turn-ended` after each send; at the
   stand bound it prints `wake: unfired` and `capture-source: unread`. Hypothesis, for you to test from the code
   and not to assume: a transport-only wrapper registers no hooks of its own, so on 2.1.326 neither
   `prompt-submitted` nor `turn-ended` is ever written, every wait runs to its bound, and the summary reads
   `unfired · unread` while the rig's OWN capture hook (the child's private `settings.json`, independent of the
   wrapper) may hold the very `source` word the start was made for. Read `viola run`'s unverified-CLI path and
   state: which event lines exist in that mode, whether `viola send` delivers, and what each of the arm's waits
   does. Then:
   - the fired wake is told by EITHER sign — the wrapper's `prompt-submitted` with no send in flight, OR a capture
     line later than the last capture line that send 1's own turn produced — and the summary says which sign it was
     (`wake-sign: event` · `capture` · `none`);
   - `capture-source`, `capture-keys` and the count of capture lines are printed from `capture.ndjson` WHATEVER
     `wake` reads, at the stand bound included; `unread` only when the file holds no line;
   - where the wrapper writes no `turn-ended`, the arm's wait after send 1 has a bound the plan names, and the
     worst-case sum for `R3-326` is shown under the watchdog as it is for `R3`.
   A rehearsal case covers the new path on the fake agent: a capture line appended by the test itself after send 1
   (the fake reads no `settings.json`) must read `wake: fired`, `wake-sign: capture`; with no such line,
   `unfired`. Its control: with the capture sign removed the case fails.
2. **Send 1's own capture line.** The typed `/loop …` is itself a UserPromptSubmit, and a `/loop` may submit more
   than one prompt in its first turn; so «the last line of `capture.ndjson`» is the fired wake's only if the arm
   knows where send 1's lines end. Say how the arm marks that point (the line count at send 1's `turn-ended`, or at
   the bound that stands for it on 2.1.326), and print the `source` word of send 1's own line(s) beside the fired
   one — a typed prompt's word is a reading too.
3. **Headroom under the watchdog.** `R3`'s worst case is put at about 590 s of 600 s, and a watchdog stop counts the
   start. Either shorten the stand (a wake asked at 1 minute needs no 300 s) or raise the watchdog for the wake
   arms, so the worst-case sum leaves at least 60 s; name the numbers.

Everything else is accepted as written: the readiness deadline and its control, the three binaries on the 20 s
line, the capture verb's closed words and its two controls, the imports arm's no-key stop, R2's explanation with no
start, the order `R3B` → `R3` → `R3-326` → `IM`, the cap as ledgered, R4's re-pin and the placeholder-hint question
onto «The 2.1.325 recorded fixture set» at the wrap. No capability claimed is right.

row.why: the overseer P5 review of p5-card-1: R3-326 on a transport-only wrapper read from the code, send 1 capture lines marked, headroom of at least 60 s under the watchdog

body: - `src/cmd/run.rs` (280-330, 560-600; read at P5, inputs#I3) — `pin_and_plugin` writes `plugin/<key>/` and the child takes `--plugin-dir` before and apart from `version_gate` (281-290), so a transport-only wrapper still registers its hooks; `sigs` is `None` on an unverified CLI (591)
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs` (171-204; read at P5) — with no signature set the gate reads a quiet screen `Ready` with no row read
- `src/run/send/classify.rs` (14-33; read at P5) — a text outside the local-command list confirms by its `prompt-submitted` whatever `cli_verified` reads

6. **The wake arms** (new `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/wake.rs`, `Arm::R3B` and `Arm::R3` in
   `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`). Both wrap the child as `arm_r2` does (`viola --home <vhome> run rig-r3 --
   <claude> --model haiku`, trust pre-seeded, no key), read every line from the start's own offset
   (decision/start-lines-read-from-start-offset), and type only through `viola send --json --file`. The request
   texts are compiled constants in two forms — `interval` (`/loop <N>m Reply with the single word ok.`) and
   `dynamic` (`/loop Reply with the single word ok, then schedule the next wake in <N> seconds.`) — read from the
   2.1.325 bundle: ScheduleWakeup is «Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode», Stop's `session_crons`
   counts «CronCreate, ScheduleWakeup, /loop» wakes, and UserPromptSubmit's `source` is `loop_wakeup` for a fired
   ScheduleWakeup and `schedule_wakeup` for any other scheduler fire (measured at P4 on the 2.1.325 install's
   bundled schema, `grep -a` on `~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.325/claude`). After each send the arm waits
   `turn-ended` whatever the send's reply word, bounded by a wake-arm turn bound of 120 s (`WAKE_TURN_BOUND`, a
   short Haiku turn; R2's 180 s `TURN_BOUND` stays R2's).
   **What a transport-only wrapper can read (inputs#I3 item 1, read from the product's code at P5):** `viola run`
   writes `plugin/<key>/` and passes `--plugin-dir` before and apart from the version gate
   (`src/cmd/run.rs:281-290`), so on an unstamped CLI the wrapper's own hooks still forward `session-start`,
   `prompt-submitted` and `turn-ended` — if that CLI runs `--plugin-dir` hooks, which on 2.1.326 is unmeasured.
   `viola send` delivers there too: with no signature set the readiness gate reads a quiet screen `Ready`
   (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs:190-191`), and a text outside the local-command list confirms by its
   `prompt-submitted` (`src/run/send/classify.rs:27-33`); only dialog decisions and the screen-signature reads are
   lost (`src/run/dialog.rs:435`, `src/cmd/run.rs:591`). So a wake arm never refuses on a missing `session-start`:
   it waits it up to the settle bound, records `session-start: seen` or `absent`, and goes on. With no
   `turn-ended`, each turn wait runs to its 120 s bound and the arm records `send-<n>-turn: unended`.
   **Send 1's own capture lines (inputs#I3 item 2):** the arm reads the line count of `<scratch root>/capture.ndjson`
   at send 1's `turn-ended`, or at its 120 s bound where none comes, as the mark (written as a number to
   `<scratch root>/send-1.mark`); it prints `send-1-capture` (the count of lines up to the mark) and
   `send-1-source` (their `source` words in order, comma-joined, `none` when no line). A line past the mark is a
   later prompt's.
   - **R3B** (R3b): send 1 the `interval` form at 30 minutes; if its `turn-ended` reads `scheduled_wakes` 0 or null,
     send 2 is the `dynamic` form at 1800 s, else send 2 is the plain text `Reply with the single word ok.`. Summary
     keys: `send-1-reply`, `send-1-wakes`, `send-2-reply`, `send-2-wakes` (the count or `null`), and
     `wake-request` — `interval`, `dynamic` or `none` (the first form whose turn end read at least 1). The rig's stop
     comes after send 2's turn ends, well before the 30-minute wake is due.
   - **R3** (R3a, R3c), taking `--wake <interval|dynamic>`: send 1 the given form at the shortest delay (1 minute /
     60 s). After send 1's mark the rig sends nothing and stands, bounded by `--stand` seconds (180 live, a wake asked
     at 1 minute) under the watchdog, until EITHER sign of the fired wake stands: the wrapper's `prompt-submitted`
     with no send in flight, or a capture line past send 1's mark. Then it waits that fired turn's `turn-ended` (120
     s bound) and stops. Summary keys: `wake` (`fired` · `unfired` at the stand bound), `wake-sign` (`event` — the
     `prompt-submitted` line came first or alone · `capture` — a capture line past the mark came first or alone ·
     `none`), `wake-origin` (the fired line's `origin`, `absent` with no line), `capture-lines` (the file's line
     count), `capture-source` and `capture-keys` (from the first capture line past the mark when one stands, else
     from the file's last line — printed WHATEVER `wake` reads, the stand bound included; `unread` only when the file
     holds no line), `send-1-capture` and `send-1-source` (above), `latency-ms` (the fired `prompt-submitted` line's
     `ts` less the fired capture line's `ms`; `unmeasured` when either is missing), `screen-ms` (the fired line's
     `ts` less the wall clock of the first frame whose reading left the idle reading after send 1's mark;
     `unmeasured` when none). At the stand bound the start reads `wake: unfired`, `wake-sign: none`, with the capture
     keys as the file holds them.
   (keeps arch S2; security S1; tests S1)

8. **Labels and verbs** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs`, `Arm::parse` / `Arm::of_label`). Live labels
   `R3B` / `R3B-2`, `R3` / `R3-2` / `R3-326`, `IM` / `IM-2`; rehearsal words `r3b`, `r3`, `im`; options `--wake` and
   `--stand <s>` (default 180). `R3-326` counts against the cap with the base starts (it ends neither in `-2`), so
   `--cap 4 --spare 3` admits exactly the founder's set through `ledger::admit`. The existing unit case on labels
   gains the new words.

9. **Rehearsals over the fake agent** (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`). One case each for `r3b`, `r3`
   (with `--stand 3`) and `im`, each in its own scratch base and credentials canary as the existing cases are, every
   rig spawn tied to the test thread (decision/no-untied-viola-spawn), every wait under the 12 s WITHIN: `r3b` reads
   `wake-request: none` with both sends' replies and turn ends read (the fake records no `session_crons`); `r3`
   reads `wake: unfired`, `wake-sign: none` at its 3 s stand and `capture-source: unread` (the fake reads no
   `settings.json`); `r3` with a capture line — the test waits for `<scratch root>/send-1.mark` under its own
   scratch base, then appends one synthetic capture line (`source` `loop_wakeup`) to that start's
   `capture.ndjson`, as the hook would — reads `wake: fired`, `wake-sign: capture`, `capture-source: loop_wakeup`;
   `im`
   reads `modal: none`, `stop: killed-no-key`, `keys: none`. Each asserts `census: 0`, `credentials: removed`,
   `scratch: absent`, `user-config: unchanged`. No fake-agent screen or fixture changes (so `cli_verify` stays out
   of the gate block). (keeps tests S1–S3; security S1, S2; obs S1; a11y S1)

- `capture-source` — entry 3, `--timeout 300`; guard: the closed `source` words (a string outside the two wake words
  reads `other`); edit: the `other` arm returns the string as given; case: the unit case on a `user` source. With
  the guard gone the case reads `user` and fails (predicted, unmeasured until implement fires it).

- `wake-capture` — entry 4, `--timeout 600`; guard: the capture sign in `wake.rs` (a capture line past send 1's
  mark tells the fired wake); edit: that branch's condition replaced by `false`; case: the `r3` rehearsal with a
  capture line. With the guard gone the start stands to its 3 s bound, reads `wake: unfired`, and the case's
  `wake-sign: capture` assertion fails (predicted, unmeasured until implement fires it); `holds` = the case FAILED
  with no TIMEOUT line (the rehearsal's own waits sit under the 12 s WITHIN, far under the binary's kill).

4. **The capture verb** (new `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/capture.rs`, wired in `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs`
   as a hidden `capture --out <file>` verb). It reads stdin through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` (an over-long input is
   `oversize`), parses one JSON object at serde_json's default depth, and appends ONE line to `<file>` (opened
   append, mode 0600 set at the open, never following a link): `{"keys":[…],"other_keys":n,"source":word,"ms":n}` —
   `keys` the sorted top-level key names that match `[a-z_]{1,40}`, `other_keys` the count of every other key name,
   `source` one closed word of `schedule_wakeup` · `loop_wakeup` · `other` (any other string) · `absent` (no key, or
   not a string), `ms` the capture's own wall clock in Unix milliseconds. No value of any key, no prompt text and no
   path is written (inputs#I2 item 3). A payload that is not one object writes `{"unread":true,"ms":n}`. It prints
   nothing and exits 0 always. Unit cases in the module cover each `source` word, a non-string `source`, the key-name
   filter, the oversize input and a non-object input (keeps tests S1; arch S2, S3). *As built:* an over-long input
   writes `{"unread":true,"oversize":true,"ms":n}`.

6. **The wake arms** (new `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/wake.rs`, `Arm::R3B` and `Arm::R3` in
   `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`). Both wrap the child as `arm_r2` does (`viola --home <vhome> run rig-r3 --
   <claude> --model haiku`, trust pre-seeded, no key), read every line from the start's own offset
   (decision/start-lines-read-from-start-offset), and type only through `viola send --json --file`. The request
   texts are compiled constants in two forms — `interval` (`/loop <N>m Reply with the single word ok.`) and
   `dynamic` (`/loop Reply with the single word ok, then schedule the next wake in <N> seconds.`) — read from the
   2.1.325 bundle: ScheduleWakeup is «Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode», Stop's `session_crons`
   counts «CronCreate, ScheduleWakeup, /loop» wakes, and UserPromptSubmit's `source` is `loop_wakeup` for a fired
   ScheduleWakeup and `schedule_wakeup` for any other scheduler fire (measured at P4 on the 2.1.325 install's
   bundled schema, `grep -a` on `~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.325/claude`). After each send the arm waits
   `turn-ended` whatever the send's reply word, bounded by a wake-arm turn bound of 120 s (`WAKE_TURN_BOUND`, a
   short Haiku turn; R2's 180 s `TURN_BOUND` stays R2's).
   **What a transport-only wrapper can read (inputs#I3 item 1, read from the product's code at P5):** `viola run`
   writes `plugin/<key>/` and passes `--plugin-dir` before and apart from the version gate
   (`src/cmd/run.rs:281-290`), so on an unstamped CLI the wrapper's own hooks still forward `session-start`,
   `prompt-submitted` and `turn-ended` — if that CLI runs `--plugin-dir` hooks, which on 2.1.326 is unmeasured.
   `viola send` delivers there too: with no signature set the readiness gate reads a quiet screen `Ready`
   (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs:190-191`), and a text outside the local-command list confirms by its
   `prompt-submitted` (`src/run/send/classify.rs:27-33`); only dialog decisions and the screen-signature reads are
   lost (`src/run/dialog.rs:435`, `src/cmd/run.rs:591`). So a wake arm never refuses on a missing `session-start`:
   it waits it up to the settle bound, records `session-start: seen` or `absent`, and goes on. With no
   `turn-ended`, each turn wait runs to its 120 s bound and the arm records `send-<n>-turn: unended`.
   **Send 1's own capture lines (inputs#I3 item 2):** the arm reads the line count of `<scratch root>/capture.ndjson`
   at send 1's `turn-ended`, or at its 120 s bound where none comes, as the mark (written as a number to
   `<scratch root>/send-1.mark`); it prints `send-1-capture` (the count of lines up to the mark) and
   `send-1-source` (their `source` words in order, comma-joined, `none` when no line). A line past the mark is a
   later prompt's.
   - **R3B** (R3b): send 1 the `interval` form at 30 minutes; if its `turn-ended` reads `scheduled_wakes` 0 or null,
     send 2 is the `dynamic` form at 1800 s, else send 2 is the plain text `Reply with the single word ok.`. Summary
     keys: `send-1-reply`, `send-1-wakes`, `send-2-reply`, `send-2-wakes` (the count or `null`), and
     `wake-request` — `interval`, `dynamic` or `none` (the first form whose turn end read at least 1). The rig's stop
     comes after send 2's turn ends, well before the 30-minute wake is due.
   - **R3** (R3a, R3c), taking `--wake <interval|dynamic>`: send 1 the given form at the shortest delay (1 minute /
     60 s). After send 1's mark the rig sends nothing and stands, bounded by `--stand` seconds (180 live, a wake asked
     at 1 minute) under the watchdog, until EITHER sign of the fired wake stands: the wrapper's `prompt-submitted`
     with no send in flight, or a capture line past send 1's mark. Then it waits that fired turn's `turn-ended` (120
     s bound) and stops. Summary keys: `wake` (`fired` · `unfired` at the stand bound), `wake-sign` (`event` — the
     `prompt-submitted` line came first or alone · `capture` — a capture line past the mark came first or alone ·
     `none`), `wake-origin` (the fired line's `origin`, `absent` with no line), `capture-lines` (the file's line
     count), `capture-source` and `capture-keys` (from the first capture line past the mark when one stands, else
     from the file's last line — printed WHATEVER `wake` reads, the stand bound included; `unread` only when the file
     holds no line), `send-1-capture` and `send-1-source` (above), `latency-ms` (the fired `prompt-submitted` line's
     `ts` less the fired capture line's `ms`; `unmeasured` when either is missing), `screen-ms` (the fired line's
     `ts` less the wall clock of the first frame whose reading left the idle reading after send 1's mark;
     `unmeasured` when none). At the stand bound the start reads `wake: unfired`, `wake-sign: none`, with the capture
     keys as the file holds them.
   (keeps arch S2; security S1; tests S1) *As built:* R3's `screen-ms` read 25411 — a frame change 25 s before the
   fire with no frame kept at it, so the number measured nothing; step 14 keeps that frame.

9. **Rehearsals over the fake agent** (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`). One case each for `r3b`, `r3`
   (with `--stand 3`) and `im`, each in its own scratch base and credentials canary as the existing cases are, every
   rig spawn tied to the test thread (decision/no-untied-viola-spawn), every wait under the 12 s WITHIN: `r3b` reads
   `wake-request: none` with both sends' replies and turn ends read (the fake records no `session_crons`); `r3`
   reads `wake: unfired`, `wake-sign: none` at its 3 s stand and `capture-source: unread` (the fake reads no
   `settings.json`); `r3` with a capture line — the test waits for `<scratch root>/send-1.mark` under its own
   scratch base, then appends one synthetic capture line (`source` `loop_wakeup`) to that start's
   `capture.ndjson`, as the hook would — reads `wake: fired`, `wake-sign: capture`, `capture-source: loop_wakeup`;
   `im`
   reads `modal: none`, `stop: killed-no-key`, `keys: none`. Each asserts `census: 0`, `credentials: removed`,
   `scratch: absent`, `user-config: unchanged`. No fake-agent screen or fixture changes (so `cli_verify` stays out
   of the gate block). (keeps tests S1–S3; security S1, S2; obs S1; a11y S1)
   *As built:* the waits use the file's own 18 s `WITHIN`, not 12 s. The 12 s `WITHIN` is the root tests' shared
   constant, sized under the root `mutants` default kill of 15 s. `rig_rehearsal` sits on neither 20 s line: it is
   not in the `ci` override filter (30 s × 4) and it falls under `mutants`' `package(viola-e2e)` override (15 s × 2),
   so 18 s stays under both kills. The fake replays `Stop.default` with `session_crons: []`, so `r3b` reads
   `send-1-wakes: 0` and `send-2-wakes: 0` (not `null`); `wake-request: none` holds as planned. The `r3` capture
   rehearsal runs under `--deadline 10`. Its fired turn never ends on the fake, so it ends by the watchdog and asserts
   the closed words and the teardown, not exit 0.

11. **The live round** (by hand, under the founder's cap, inputs#I2 item 2), in this order: `R3B` → `R3` → `R3-326`
    → `IM` (inputs#I2 item 8). Before the round: the round probes (both installs by path, the census at 0) and a
    plain `cargo build --bin viola` whose content key the wake starts' `viola-build` must equal. Each start is
    ledgered by the rig with the clock's time before it is made, to `evidence/live-starts.ndjson`; a start the rig
    refuses for the token window (`refused: token-window`, exit 3, before the ledger line) is uncounted — stop and
    say so, set no timer. `R3B` first: if it reads `wake-request: none`, the round stops before `R3` and the report
    says so (inputs#I2 item 8). Otherwise `R3` and `R3-326` take `--wake` as `R3B` printed it. A reading that «did not
    show» (`wake-request: none`, `wake: unfired`, `modal: none`) is a reading, never a lost start; a spare is spent
    only where the start's shape itself was wrong, the report naming which (inputs#I2 item 2). `R3-326` has no spare.
    Then write `evidence/live-starts.md`: per start its clock time, binary, summary line and readings, every one as
    closed words.
    *As built:* the four base starts fired, no spare (`evidence/live-starts.md`, `live-starts.ndjson`, `round-*.txt`):
    `R3B` green (`send-1-wakes: 1`, `wake-request: interval`); `R3` read RED on `contains 'user-config: unchanged'` —
    `user-config: changed` at 16:40:20Z, a host writer rewriting `~/.claude.json` about once a minute with no rig alive
    (`evidence/user-config-writer.md`), which the stamp-only witness could not attribute; its readings stand (fired
    wake, no `source` key, `latency-ms: 3`). It is recorded as read and NOT re-fired or re-worded (inputs#I6 item 4).
    `R3-326` green (same readings on 2.1.326, `session-start: seen`); `IM` green (`modal: imports`, `stop:
    killed-no-key`).

12. **The user-config witness by the rig's own marks** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs`, and `start` /
    `finish` in `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` where the summary's `user-config` is put; the founder's own answer,
    inputs#I6 item 1). The whole-file stamp (sha + mtime, `isolate::stamp`) is read before and after as now. When it
    held, the word is `unchanged`; absent before and after, `absent`. When it moved, the rig reads the file ONCE:
    through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` (over → `unread`); a symbolic link at the path is followed only when its canonical
    target lies under the user's home (`HOME`), else `unread`; absent or unreadable → `unread`. The bytes are searched
    for exactly two needles, each a fixed byte string the rig made: the PATH needle, the canonical scratch root (the
    child's cwd and private config lie under it, so any path the child wrote holds it); the ID needle, the session id
    of the child the rig started — the `agent_session_id` of the first `session-start` a wrapped arm (`R2` · `R3B` ·
    `R3`) reads off its own instance's `events.ndjson`, kept only when `viola_agent_claude::is_session_id` accepts
    it. An unwrapped arm (`R1` · `IM` · `Hold`), or a wrapped one that read no `session-start`, learns no id: the path
    needle alone decides. Words: a needle found → `changed-by-rig` (RED: the start's exit is 1); none found →
    `changed-by-others`. The summary prints `user-config: {word}` and `needles: {1|2}`. Nothing of the file's content
    is kept, copied, printed, logged or written to a record: the read bytes are dropped after the search. The decision
    is a plain function over `(before, after, the read, the needles)`, unit cases in `isolate.rs`: stamp held →
    `unchanged`; stamp moved, no mark → `changed-by-others`; stamp moved, the path mark present → `changed-by-rig`;
    stamp moved, the id mark present → `changed-by-rig`; stamp moved, no id needle, an id-shaped text present →
    `changed-by-others` (`needles: 1`); the file absent or unreadable after a moved stamp → `unread`; a link out of the
    home → `unread` (keeps tests S1; security S1).

13. **The witness rehearsed on a stand-in** (`crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`). The rehearsals' `--user-config`
    is the case's own stand-in file, never the user's. `rig_reads_the_user_config_before_and_after`'s rewrite (no
    mark) now reads `changed-by-others`. A new case runs the `hold` arm, waits for its first frame, writes into the
    stand-in a JSON value holding that start's canonical scratch root path (the one dir under the case's scratch
    base), SIGINTs the rig, and reads `user-config: changed-by-rig`, `needles: 1`, exit 1, with no path in its stdout.
    `r3b` and `r3` read `needles: 2` (the fake's recorded SessionStart id is of the session-id shape) and
    `user-config: unchanged`.

14. **R3's frame at the screen change, and its wake count** (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/wake.rs`, `arm_r3`). At the
    first frame whose closed reading leaves the post-mark reading, the arm keeps that frame as `left-idle` (local,
    as every kept frame), so a `screen-ms` reading names the frame it measured. The arm also puts `send-1-wakes`
    (send 1's `turn-ended` `scheduled_wakes`, the count or `null`), as `R3B` does.

15. **The `R3D` label** (`Arm::of_label` in `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`): `R3D` maps to `Arm::R3`; the label
    unit case gains it. `ledger::admit` counts `R3D` against the base cap (no `-2`), so its entry passes `--cap 5
    --spare 3`: the four spent base starts plus `R3D`, the three spares unspent.

16. **The `R3D` live start** (by hand, inputs#I6 items 2, 5): ONE start, NO spare, after every fake-agent entry is
    green; its round steps first (the rig census at 0, a plain `cargo build --bin viola` whose key `viola-build` must
    equal), ledgered by the rig with the clock's time before it is made, no key. Shape: send 1 types the `dynamic`
    form at the shortest delay, `/loop Reply with the single word ok, then schedule the next wake in 60 seconds.`
    The dynamic form is UNMEASURED on this host: `R3B` tried `interval` first, it read 1, and the arm stopped there.
    The expectation rests on the 2.1.325 bundle (step 6): ScheduleWakeup is «Schedule when to resume work in /loop
    dynamic mode», Stop's `session_crons` counts ScheduleWakeup wakes, and the schema names a fired ScheduleWakeup's
    `source` `loop_wakeup`. So send 1's turn should read `send-1-wakes: 1`, and the wake should fire about 60 s later,
    inside the 180 s stand. If the model calls no ScheduleWakeup, the start reads `wake: unfired` at the stand bound,
    with `send-1-wakes` as read (0 or `null`): a READING, never a lost start. Bounds as card 2 revised them: stand
    180 s, watchdog `--deadline 900`, worst case 662 s (Implementation notes), entry `timeout` 1200 s. Its readings and
    the new witness's word are appended to `evidence/live-starts.md`.

17. **The `ready-deadline` control the tool can fire** (`.config/nextest.toml` untouched; a gate entry only). The
    stopped run's control read UNREPRODUCED in `gate.py control`'s clone. Entry 6 is package-scoped, so the clone
    built no `viola-fake-agent`, and the case's copy of it panicked `NotFound` (testing.md 2026-11-13). The run then
    held the control by hand over a whole-workspace clone (`evidence/control-2.txt`, kept as that firing's
    evidence). A new non-leg entry builds the workspace with the fake agent first (`cargo build -q --workspace
    --features viola/fake-agent`), then runs the case under nextest's default profile (no kill line). `gate.py
    control` fires the `ready-deadline` control on that entry. A harness layer (`run --integration`) is no fit: it
    runs the `ci` profile, whose 20 s line would kill the guard-removed case (measured 20.340 s) as a TIMEOUT.
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/wake.rs` — the R3B and R3 arms; revision 1: the session id learned for the witness, R3's `left-idle` frame and `send-1-wakes` (step 14)

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — the new `Arm` variants and their dispatch, the imports arm, the no-key stop; revision 1: the needles carried to `finish`, the witness word and `needles`, the `R3D` label (steps 12, 15)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs` — the capture hook in the private config, the imports seed; revision 1: the mark-search witness and its unit cases (step 12)
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — the three rehearsals; revision 1: the stand-in mark case, `changed-by-others`, `needles` (step 13)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/session.rs` — the field at its literal
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-harness.rs` — the field at its literals

No boot-path touchpoint (no `src/` file, no wrapper start path): the harness smoke is not a gate here. The live legs
are the round; every other entry runs on the fake agent. Entry 20 (revision 1) is the deadline control's entry: it
builds the workspace with the fake agent, then runs the case under nextest's default profile, which has no kill line,
so a removed guard reads as the case failing, never a TIMEOUT; it stands after the round's span (entries 9–19), so the
round's pre-flight finds no non-leg entry inside it. Entries 13–16 are the four starts already fired (revision 1):
none is re-fired; entry 14's recorded red stands as its disposition names (its `note`). Entries 17–19 are `R3D`'s
round steps and its start, fired by `gate.py run --live-legs --entry 19`. No manifest changes, so `cargo deny check`
is not listed.

- `ready-deadline` — entry 20 (revision 1; was entry 6, which the tool's clone could not build for: UNREPRODUCED,
  then held by hand over a whole-workspace clone — in place PASS 2.303 s, removed FAIL 20.340 s, no TIMEOUT,
  `evidence/control-2.txt`), `--timeout 1200` (the clone's whole-workspace build, then the case); guard: `start`
  reads `opts.ready_deadline`; edit in `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/boot.rs`: `opts.ready_deadline` →
  `INSTANCE_DEADLINE` at the wait; case `boot_that_never_gets_ready_times_out_and_stops_its_supervisor`. With the
  guard gone the boot waits the 20 s constant and the case's wall assertion (below 10 s) fails about 20 s in, under
  nextest's default profile (no kill line); `holds` = the case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line.

- `capture-keys` — entry 3, `--timeout 300`; guard: the key-name filter in `capture.rs` (a name outside
  `[a-z_]{1,40}` counted in `other_keys`, never listed); edit: the filter's predicate replaced by `true`; case: the
  unit case on an off-pattern key name. With the guard gone that name is listed in `keys` and the case's assertion
  fails. Read `holds` by the stopped run (`evidence/control-1.txt`).

- `capture-source` — entry 3, `--timeout 300`; guard: the closed `source` words (a string outside the two wake words
  reads `other`); edit: the `other` arm returns the string as given; case: the unit case on a `user` source. With
  the guard gone the case reads `user` and fails. Read `holds` by the stopped run (`evidence/control-1.txt`).

- `wake-capture` — entry 4, `--timeout 600`; guard: the capture sign in `wake.rs` (a capture line past send 1's
  mark tells the fired wake); edit: that branch's condition replaced by `false`; case: the `r3` rehearsal with a
  capture line. With the guard gone the start stands to its 3 s bound, reads `wake: unfired`, and the case's
  `wake-sign: capture` assertion fails; `holds` = the case FAILED with no TIMEOUT line (the rehearsal's own waits
  sit under its 18 s WITHIN, far under the binary's kill). Read `holds` by the stopped run (`evidence/control-3.txt`).

- `user-config-mark` — entry 3, `--timeout 300` (revision 1, inputs#I6 item 3); guard: the mark search in
  `isolate.rs` (a needle found in the moved file reads `changed-by-rig`); edit: the search's found-predicate replaced
  by `false`; case: the unit case «stamp moved, the path mark present». With the guard gone that case reads
  `changed-by-others` and fails (predicted, unmeasured until implement fires it); `holds` = the case FAILED.

- Crate dependency direction is enforced by manifests: `viola-core` depends on no viola crate; `viola-pty` knows no agent; `viola-hyprland` is the one compositor seam (queries and dispatches only through its closed request set), sync and tokio-free, depending on `viola-core` alone among viola crates; only `viola-agent-claude` knows Claude payload shapes, including those of `claude agents --json` (except the test-only live rig in `viola-e2e`, which reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload, never a value); among the product crates only `viola-mcp` enables tokio (`rt`), and `viola-channel` lists it optional behind its `tokio` feature (the `TokioClient`), which `viola-mcp` enables; the root bin holds the subcommand dispatch, the run pump and the wheel, all of which consume only normalised events.

The only crate that knows Claude Code (one test-only exception: the live rig in `viola-e2e` reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload, never a value). It parses hook payloads tolerantly and maps each hook to a normalised kind. It maps dialog answers to decision bodies (S3 / S7 / S8) and applies the R8 `CLAUDE*` strip. It resolves the child program (`resolve_program`: a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`) and holds the Claude-specific half of the CLI version gate: the capability ledger rows (compiled) with their `viola verify` checks, `parse_version`, the stamp merge and `verified` verdict, and the fixture scrub. The gate's spawn is the root bin's `run::version_gate`; the stamps I/O is `viola_state::stamps`. It keeps the vt100 screen signatures (readiness gate), parses, in the pure `agents` module, a `claude agents --json` answer (`parse` into rows or a closed `AgentsFailure`, `oversize` · `malformed`; the read itself is the root bin's `run::agents`), and normalises `prompt-submitted` (removes the long-paste wrapper, then reverses tag escaping; classifies `origin` driver/human/harness). It also holds the resume shapes `viola revive` launches with (`viola verify`'s Run E is the second caller of `resume_args(id, false)`): `PROGRAM` (`claude`), `RESUME_FLAG`, `FORK_SESSION_FLAG`, `is_session_id` (36 characters, hyphens at offsets 8, 13, 18, 23, ASCII hex elsewhere) and `resume_args(id, fork)`; it is the one product home of the two flag literals.
